subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Right knee pain and need for knee replacement surgery
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 74 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because I need to have my right knee replaced this summer, and I need to make sure my heart condition is stable before the surgery. Doctor: Could you please provide more details about your heart condition, including any diagnoses, medications, or previous treatments? Patient: I have chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction. I was on furosemide before, but they switched me to torsemide 20 milligrams by mouth daily. I also take lisinopril, which they increased to 10 milligrams daily. I haven't been on a potassium supplement, but I do have some leg cramps sometimes. Doctor: Could you describe the current pain level in your right knee and how it affects your daily activities? Patient: My knee pain is manageable most of the time, but it does bother me when I try to walk longer distances or go up and down stairs. It's been making it harder to keep up with my gardening, which I really enjoy. I'm hoping the surgery will help me get back to doing more of the things I love. Doctor: Could you please provide the results of your most recent echocardiogram, blood pressure readings, and any recent laboratory tests such as BNP or electrolyte levels? Additionally, could you share the findings from your physical examination and any imaging or lab tests related to your knee condition? Patient: I don't have the results of my most recent echocardiogram on hand, but I was told my heart function is stable enough for the surgery. My blood pressure has been okay, and my latest blood work showed my potassium is 3.9, which is steady. I haven't had any recent imaging for my knee, just some discussions about the surgery plans. Doctor: Could you please describe any current symptoms related to your knee, such as pain, swelling, or difficulty with movement?
